Standalone status rests on the US manual (setup asks only for the Empires disc; importing DW5/XL data is optional and only possible before an Empires save exists) and on PALGN's 'standalone add-on pack' wording, quoted via Metacritic. Wikipedia calls it an expansion.

No officer loyalty stat is described in the US manual or the sources used. The article only covers recruitment, hiring captured officers for 400 to 4000 gold, bribing with items, and defection policies.

The policy names (e.g. Weaponsmith, Long Alliance) are confirmed only from the Consult screenshot. In the archive.org OCR the manual's policy-name column did not come through, so the article describes policies by their manual descriptions.
Co-Optimus reproduces Koei's blurb claiming 75 policies, 25 of them new. That figure was not independently verified and is not used in the article.

The GamesRadar (Sewart) page shows no score or platform. Metacritic lists a GamesRadar+ 70 for PS2 with a different excerpt, so that score is not attributed to Sewart. The IGN review was not located. The Famitsu score is taken from Wikipedia, not from Famitsu directly.

Rejected media: the Skyscraper screenshot 8b984c0d... duplicates the DW5 base-game frame. The libretro Named_Snaps (sha1 6ede94cf...) shows a generic DW5-style battle (Cheng Yuanzhi, 50 K.O. message) that cannot be tied to Empires. The libretro Named_Titles is a French PAL title screen ('APPUYER SUR START'). MobyGames was behind a Cloudflare challenge, WorthPlaying's press images return HTML, and the GamePro gallery images are not archived. No genuine strategy-map (territory map) screenshot of the PS2 version was found; the Consult screen and the manual's Orders page illustrate the strategy layer instead.
Session/campaign length is an authorial inference from the rules (25 areas, one battle per turn, reviewers' roughly 20-minute battles). No HowLongToBeat-style data for the PS2 version was used.
Redump verification of serial SLUS-21398 was not completed (redump.org quicksearch returned an error page). The serial comes from the PCSX2 GameIndex NTSC-U entry.

sources.reviewedEdition: NTSC-U SLUS-21873: compat 5, no fixes listed; upstream desktop data, not a tested result

notes: Nothing was played or launched.

Pilot/suit freedom: Wikipedia's 'any combination' is overstated. The PS2 manual gates suits by full part sets, licences (Mission Mode License Missions) and Newtype-only restrictions; Versus skips licences. Exact starting rosters per mode weren't verified.
The manual says Mission Mode has 'seven different categories' but names six. The fan wiki's seventh, Download Missions, is PS3/360-only.

Mobile armor list: only the Psyco Gundam (product description) and the Big Zam (fan wiki roster, MA-08) are named. A fuller community list (Psyco Gundam Mk-II, Quin Mantha, Alpha Azieru, Dark Gundam) surfaced in search summaries, but PlayStationTrophies/TrueAchievements pages were blocked by Cloudflare/JS, so it is unverified and not used.
Smash Attack's armor-breaking role and Partial Destruction come from the fan wiki, not the manual. The manual only lists long-press Square = Smash Attack.
That parts never change a suit's weapons or silhouette is an inference from the manual's descriptions (stats, SP level, skills), labelled as such in the article.

PS2 online play: GameSpot's 2011 game-stats box lists 'Online Modes: Competitive' for the PS2 page, but the PS2 manual describes only local Versus and IGN's PS2 review mentions only split-screen. The article says only that online play is documented for PS3/360 (IGN PS3/360 review). PS2 online status is unresolved.
GameZone's 6.6 review is filed under PS2 but mentions achievement points; the platform actually played is unclear.
IGN's PS3/360 score wasn't checked; only that review's multiplayer statement is used.

Lead screenshot: PS2 provenance rests on ScreenScraper/libretro cataloguing plus 4:3 SD pixels; the region (NTSC-U vs PAL) is undeterminable. The libretro PS2 USA snap is the same frame, not independent evidence.
No substantial later critical reassessment of the PS2 version was found.

The PCSX2 GameIndex has no compat rating for SLUS-21803; the PAL SLES-55382 rating of 5 is not evidence for the US disc.

No English PS2 gameplay frame was obtained from Skyscraper, libretro or review galleries: the Skyscraper and libretro snaps are Japanese, GameZone gallery images couldn't be retrieved because the Internet Archive was temporarily offline, and MobyGames/GameSpot/GameFAQs galleries were blocked. The lead image is therefore a manual-printed screenshot.
The manual date is year-only (2008), from the printed copyright. Survival's preset ('fixed') character data is interpreted from the manual's rule text.

Wikipedia is the source for the IGN PSP score (5.2), the Dream Mode 28-stage count, the PSP-port additions and the Japanese sales figure; those primary pages weren't opened. No substantial later reassessment was found.
The Metacritic PS2 aggregate of 52 from 9 reviews was confirmed on the live page and in a 2014 Wayback capture.
